sub_scenario.one_line: logistics dispatcher: planned desk above the exception desk

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the constraint sheet and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The route plan review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Single exceptions between plans are absorbable, even welcome; they break monotony.
Volume is the poison, not exceptions.
Dose makes the poison, exactly.
Someone new shadowed me in the dispatch office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the dock slots into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On the planned-route desk I sequenced eighty deliveries with a constraint sheet and the fleet ran a full week without a missed window.
The sheet holds the whole picture.
Eighty stops fit in no one's head, including mine.
I thrive on the planned desk even during crunch; volume alone does not shake me.
Complexity under structure is your terrain.
My favorite terrain.
I archived last cycle's notes on the route plan and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My constraint-sheet method needs about six quiet minutes per replan; I have timed it for years.
A known cycle time.
A cycle the live desk never grants.
A vendor call about the constraint sheet ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the dispatch office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the dock slots.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the route plan records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Covering the live-exception desk in April, radio calls stacked while I re-planned, and I assigned two drivers to the same dock slot; both sat idle for an hour.
Mid-replan interruptions caused the double-booking?
I was four exceptions deep and lost the board state.
I sketched next week's plan for the dock slots before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the constraint sheet updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Exception volume triples in weather season, which is exactly when I would hold that desk.
Peak switching at peak stakes.
The rota gods have humor.
I compared two options for the route plan tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the dispatch office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The bid sheet wants my desk ranking for next season: planned-route desk versus live-exception desk. What order do I submit?
